data.name: Logix TUI keyboard commands and assignment standard

specification.status: Accepted specification baseline summarized from the keyboard proposal; implementation and conformance remain to be validated.
specification.scope: Native Logix-aware editors, forms, spreadsheets, file views and application lifecycle. Legacy CP/M console and Unix-compatible terminal sessions retain explicitly selected compatibility profiles.
specification.historical_context: Forward-looking alternative-history design at the TUI launch; later DOS, Windows and Linux conventions are design references, not claimed historical 1978 standards.
assignment_rules: Arrows navigate; Ctrl modifies navigation granularity; Shift extends selection using the same movement destination.
Ctrl supplies editing/document commands; Alt supplies menu and system actions. System-reserved commands cannot be rebound by applications.
Dispatch stable logical command identifiers separately from physical keys. Resolve focused control, active dialog, application and system ownership explicitly.
Show shortcuts in menus/help; disabled or unavailable commands report their state. Compatibility profiles are explicit, visible and never silently mixed.

navigation.scope: only after higher-priority transient UI is dismissed

editing.keys: Ctrl+X; alias Shift+Delete in text editors only

documents.scope: line, cell or record in a document; context named in UI

focus_and_lifecycle.scope: system close request with unsaved-work checks
cooperative cancellation; not immediate forced termination

behavior.selection: Fixed anchor and moving caret. Plain Left/Right collapses to the corresponding selection edge without an extra step; vertical motion retains the preferred column. Home/End target displayed-line boundaries.
behavior.boundaries: Shared word-boundary implementation groups letters, digits and underscore; freeze punctuation/whitespace traversal in conformance examples. Plain-text paragraphs are separated by blank lines; structured editors use paragraph objects.
behavior.clipboard: Copy/Cut without a selection does nothing. Cut removes data only after clipboard transfer succeeds. Delete preserves clipboard. Typing or pasting replaces a selection as one undoable operation; allocation failure must not partially destroy selected content.
behavior.saving: Report Save success only after successful completion; retain modified state on failure. Close offers Save/Discard/Cancel for modified content; Quit checks every modified document.
behavior.contexts: Spreadsheet navigation selects cells until cell-edit mode, which uses text rules. Editor Tab indents and Shift+Tab unindents; form Tab traverses focus. F6 leaves a multiline editor. Esc acts on only one innermost context per press.
behavior.overwrite: Insertion mode by default. Overwrite is an explicit visibly indicated option; bare Insert does not toggle it by default.
behavior.optional_commands: Formatting Ctrl+B/I/U is optional in capable editors. Whole-line deletion, duplication, transpose and rectangular selection remain menu commands outside the common shortcut core.
behavior.platform_limits: Aurelia remains single-foreground. Alt+Tab exposes the supported launcher/switch mechanism and does not promise concurrent applications or preserved running state. Query lifecycle capabilities on each host.

terminal_compatibility.selection: Explicit terminal profile; no selection-dependent change between Ctrl+C Copy and Interrupt.

bindings.scope: depends on terminal mode and pending input; not unconditional Quit

terminal_compatibility.flow_control: Native TUI Ctrl+S/Q are Save/Quit and must not be intercepted by software flow control. Terminal sessions may preserve configured XON/XOFF behavior.
terminal_compatibility.legacy_profiles: Optional WordStar/Emacs profiles are whole opt-in keymaps, not conflicting default aliases. Legacy CP/M control-character semantics are preserved outside native TUI contexts.

input_contract.events: Key identity plus Ctrl/Shift/Alt modifier state; text translation is separate. Preserve Ctrl+Shift navigation and Ctrl+Shift letter distinctions.
input_contract.terminal_fallback: Traditional byte terminals can conflate Tab/Ctrl+I, Enter/Ctrl+M, Esc/Ctrl+[, Backspace/Ctrl+H and shifted Ctrl letters. Advertise capabilities and offer menu equivalents rather than ambiguous shortcut promises.
input_contract.qualification: Existing keyboard exact layout, event encoding, rollover and firmware remain engineering gates; required controls are conformance requirements, not a qualified new hardware revision.
